raw.question: Who counts as a child under this law?
raw.answer: A child is defined as an individual who has not completed the age of eighteen years.
raw.plain_language: Under this law, a child is anyone under eighteen years old.
raw.original_clause:
[Section 2(f)] (f) "child" means an individual who has not completed the age of eighteen
years;

raw.question: What does an organisation have to do if it suffers a personal data breach?
raw.answer: An organisation must give the Board and each affected Data Principal intimation of the breach in the prescribed form and manner.
raw.plain_language: If your organization experiences a personal data breach, you must inform the Board and the affected individuals promptly, following the specific guidelines set by the government.
raw.original_clause:
[Section 8(6)] (6) In the event of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall give the Board and
each affected Data Principal, intimation of such breach in such form and manner as may be
prescribed.
raw.disclaimer: This is general information about the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, not legal advice. Check the original text or consult a qualified lawyer before acting on it.

raw.question: Can I take back my consent later, and how easy does that have to be?
raw.answer: Yes, you can withdraw your consent at any time, and it should be as easy as giving it.
raw.plain_language: You can revoke your consent whenever you want, and it should be just as easy as when you first gave it.
raw.original_clause:
[Section 6(4)] (4) Where consent given by the Data Principal is the basis of processing of personal
data, such Data Principal shall have the right to withdraw her consent at any time, with the
ease of doing so being comparable to the ease with which such consent was given.
raw.disclaimer: This is general information about the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, not legal advice. Check the original text or consult a qualified lawyer before acting on it.

raw.question: What is the maximum fine for not taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent a data breach?
raw.answer: The maximum fine for not taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent a data breach is two hundred and fifty crore rupees.
raw.plain_language: If a Data Fiduciary does not take reasonable security measures to protect personal data, they could be fined up to two hundred and fifty crore rupees.
raw.original_clause:
[Schedule, item 1] 1. Breach: Breach in observing the obligation of Data Fiduciary to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach under sub-section (5) of section 8.
Penalty: May extend to two hundred and fifty crore rupees.
raw.disclaimer: This is general information about the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, not legal advice. Check the original text or consult a qualified lawyer before acting on it.

raw.question: What information must be given in the notice before my consent is asked for?
raw.answer: The notice must inform the Data Principal about the personal data to be processed, the purpose of processing, and how to exercise rights and make complaints.
raw.plain_language: The Data Fidu002cciary must give a notice to the Data Principal that tells them what personal information will be used, why it's being used, and how they can exercise their rights and complain if needed.
raw.original_clause:
[Section 6(10)] (10) Where a consent given by the Data Principal is the basis of processing of
personal data and a question arises in this regard in a proceeding, the Data Fiduciary shall
be obliged to prove that a notice was given by her to the Data Principal and consent was
given by such Data Principal to the Data Fiduciary in accordance with the provisions of this
Act and the rules made thereunder.

raw.question: Is targeted advertising aimed at children allowed?
raw.answer: No, targeted advertising aimed at children is not allowed.
raw.plain_language: A Data Fiduciary cannot track children or show them targeted ads.
raw.original_clause:
[Section 9(3)] (3) A Data Fiduciary shall not undertake tracking or behavioural monitoring of children
or targeted advertising directed at children.

raw.question: How quickly must a company reply to my grievance?
raw.answer: The Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager must respond to grievances within a prescribed period.
raw.plain_language: The company has to reply to your grievance within a time frame set by the government rules.
raw.original_clause:
[Section 13(2)] (2) The Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager shall respond to any grievances referred
to in sub-section (1) within such period as may be prescribed from the date of its receipt for
all or any class of Data Fiduciaries.
raw.disclaimer: This is general information about the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, not legal advice. Check the original text or consult a qualified lawyer before acting on it.

raw.question: What duties do I have as a Data Principal?
raw.answer: As a Data Principal, you must comply with all applicable laws, ensure authenticity of information, and have means for grievance redressal.
raw.plain_language: You must follow all laws, make sure your personal data is real, and have a way to complain if something goes wrong.
raw.original_clause:
[Section 15] A Data Principal shall perform the following duties, namely:—
(a) comply with the provisions of all applicable laws for the time being in force
while exercising rights under the provisions of this Act;
(b) to ensure not to impersonate another person while providing her personal
data for a specified purpose;
(c) to ensure not to suppress any material information while providing her
personal data for any document, unique identifier, proof of identity or proof of address
issued by the State or any of its instrumentalities;
(d) to ensure not to register a false or frivolous grievance or complaint with a
Data Fiduciary or the Board; and
(e) to furnish only such information as is verifiably authentic, while exercising
the right to correction or erasure under the provisions of this Act or the rules made
thereunder.

[Section 13(1)] (1)A Data Principal shall have the right to have readily available means of grievance
redressal provided by a Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager in respect of any act or omission
of such Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager regarding the performance of its obligations in
relation to the personal data of such Data Principal or the exercise of her rights under the
provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder.

raw.question: How long do I have to appeal against an order of the Data Protection Board, and to whom?
raw.answer: You have sixty days to appeal against an order of the Data Protection Board, and the appeal must be filed before the Appellate Tribunal.
raw.plain_language: You must appeal within 60 days, and the appeal goes to the Appellate Tribunal.
raw.original_clause:
[Section 29(6)] (6) The appeal filed before the Appellate Tribunal under sub-section (1) shall be dealt
with by it as expeditiously as possible and endeavour shall be made by it to dispose of the
appeal finally within six months from the date on which the appeal is presented to it.

[Section 29(2)] (2) Every appeal under sub-section (1) shall be filed within a period of sixty days from
the date of receipt of the order or direction appealed against and it shall be in such form and
manner and shall be accompanied by such fee as may be prescribed.
